newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Malaysia firm to build $1 billion town in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia firm to build $1 billion town in Cambodia.

text.p: Malaysia's SungeiWay Group will build a $1 billion town on a large tract of swampland facing Phnom Penh under a joint venture deal signed Monday with the Cambodian government, executives and officials said.

Secretary of State for Finance Chanthol Sun said the joint venture company, Sunway City Cambodia Ltd, would reclaim 400 hectares (988 acres) of swamp for the new town on the Chroy Changvar peninsula, across the Tonle Sap River from the capital.
SungeiWay holds an 80 percent stake in the venture and will provide funding for the construction of residential, commercial, industrial and resort areas on land provided by the government.

"The estimated cost will be about $1 billion," said Chanthol Sun. He added that the project would take 10-15 years to complete and would represent one of the biggest foreign investments in Cambodia since rival factions signed a peace accord in 1991.
Initial paid up capital for the project is $10 million.
A SungeiWay official said studies on the reclamation could start later this year.

"It is one of the most exciting (foreign investment) projects allowing for the development of Cambodia," First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh told Reuters after the signing, adding that it would also help cut land speculation.
